The Famous Cape Minstrels

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It's not just a pretty story

Summary:
The Kaapse Klopse Parade is South Africa's biggest carnival and once again the streets of Cape Town will be filled with about 80 000 brightly colored minstrels and Cape Town comes to a halt. But there is drama each year - funding, power struggles exemplified by the fact that this parade is taking place ten days later than it's usual date.

But all of this is lost and not understood by a ten year old young boy who lives in the community and who dreams of this big day. We follow that boy throughout the day. Whilst he is the thread to the story we explore some of the controversies surrounding the parade every year.

Further information:
For example, the person holding the purse strings this year has received over 20 million rand for the parade is a very powerful man - in fact he is an ex gangster with a criminal record. None of the various troops dare to challenge him because their troop with be ousted from the organization.

Where does all the money go? Very few know that he has a factory that provides some of the uniforms and people are forced to buy these uniforms from him. It is in the contract. Meanwhile the City of Cape Town is demanding an audit from Mr, Stemmet. The ex gangster with time in jail, sneers at the 3 million given to them by the City of Cape Town and promises to provide an audit at some stage to the City of Cape Town. In the meantime, attempts have been made to get an audit from the lottery board who this year gave a whopping 16 million for this one day parade. They wont release this audit until they are given permission by this Stemmet man. Naturally he hasn't given permission.

So behind all the glitz and glamor there is more than meets the eye. Of course the young boy who we feature will be oblivious to all of this. We investigate.

Press Release:


Cape Minstrels
The annual Cape minstrel parade is an institution in Cape Town. But beneath the veneer of smiling faces and brightly coloured costumes, a massive row is brewing over the allocation of lottery millions. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


Cape town…and its been a long night for these campers. But the wait will be well worth it, for this is South Africa’s most colorful carnival.

Like his father, his grand and great grandfather did, young Thaaqib starts the day with having his face painted. All around the cape Peninsula, parents and their children are lining up to have theirs done…

Here in the Bokaap where Thaaqib lives, his mom is rushing to have his uniform ironed.

Interview Faa-iekah Ryland
My son is really excited… He lives for this day; he did not even sleep last night.

A proud young man! His excitement his shared by 1000’s of other children eager to get going.

Bonita: What is the best past of the carnival for you?
Thaaqib: When you in the streets, and mostly 1000’s of people are watching.

Then it’s a quick walk to board a waiting. Bus. Once the whole troop is aboard, the bus will drive these minstrels to perform elsewhere in the peninsula and then offload them at the top of town to join the parade

Link: Its an institution here, the Cape Town Carnival, the Kaapse Klospe is a unique event but every year its mired in controversy, mudslinging and petty politics.

Kevin Momberg: We get absolutely zilch, in terms of money, for the captains, nothing.
JP Smith: Since my involvement with the council in 2000 I don’t think there has been a year when it has not been drama free:
Dolly: but these people will never talk cause they are scared.

Link: Fortunately for the minstrels, the people of Cape Town, upcountry visitors, international tourists, it somehow resolves itself and the as you can see the show must go on.

58 individual troops, numbering tens of thousands of minstrels, take to the streets with exotic names such as the fabulous Woodstock starlight’s, the suburban boys and the lavender superstars.

We spotted Thaaqib amongst the dancing troops, proud to part of this heritage.

Bonita: Why do you do this?
Minstrel: Because you know what? Our ancestors did it. Our ancestors, they did, it’s in our blood to do this things my sweetheart.

The origin of the carnival stretches as far back as the 1800's when slaves from District 6 were allowed one day off each year and that was the 2nd of January.
Today the Cape Minstrels fall under three associations - The Cape Town Minstrel Carnival Association, The Kaapse Klopse Karnival Association and the Cape District Minstrel Board - often at loggerheads with each other.
This year the minstrels, except for the Cape District Minstrel Board, wanted full control over the parade, an event previously organized by the city of Cape Town. Kevin Momberg is the CEO of the association, and NPO with the most troops.

Kevin Momberg: We told them we want to run our own organization. Why must people come in and, we come to Cape Town as guests on our own march.


Bonita: So why this year did the City of Cape Town hand over the p0rganaistion of the event to the minstrels?
JP Smith: I think precisely to try and avert the to and fro for the three months preceding the even every year.


The trouble started this year when the event, known as the The Tweede Nuwe Jaar, which normally takes place on the 2nd of January had to be postponed because this date fell on the prophets birthday. The parade was set for a weekday but this would cause major logistical problems and it was cancelled. The 17th of January was then decided upon but a few days before the actual event, more drama

Bonita: So why did the city decide to g public about payments not having been made just a few days before the event?
JP Smith: When we were reviewing the logistics for the 17th, we determined that payments had not been made to either the suppliers of the toilets or the fencing and that therefore they would not be supplying those services on the 17th, which meant in effect we would see another cancellation.

Kevin Momberg was upset that the city had gone public.

Kevin Momberg: But we had an agreement that we will pay them and we paid 70% upfront to both the toilets and the fencing guys that they were so going on about.

But the contract he signed with service providers stated that services would only be delivered after a 100 per cent payment upfront. He duly paid them the full amount. The city then issued an event permit.

Link: All of this costs a lot of money. Uniforms need to be brought, infrastructure for events such as these needs to be paid for, busses transport, you name it, so where does all the money come from.

To buy all of the paraphernalia such as the uniforms, hats, brollies and instruments, Troops fundraise themselves and some are able to secure private sponsorships. The city and the western cape government; knowing how much these events cost from past experience, say they provided enough funds for the parade to Kevin Momberg and his chairman Richard Stemmet to share with the other associations.

Link: their around 6 Million Rand grant from the City of Cape Town and provincial government is sufficient to cover the costs of the event in full but we have now discovered that huge amounts of additional funding has been pouring in.

Meet Shahieda "Dolly" Thole who heads up the association with the smallest amount of troops - the Cape District Minstrel Board. She approached the lotto last year to try and secure finding for her troops but was turned down.

Shahieda Thole: I was told that my application is declined and I asked on what basis and they said because there is a mother body in the WC that is receiving money for the whole of the Western Cape, Minstrel teams,

She asked for proof and she was flabbergasted to find that the lotto had paid out just over 41 million rand to Kevin Momberg’s associations. What was that money for?

Shahieda Thole: Nobody knows, only he will know, only Richard Stemmet. He knows and Momberg, they will know what they are doing with the money.

We found out last week that the lotto board had in fact given the this association even more


Bonita: The Cape Town Minstrel Carnival Assocation recieved 57 million rand from the lotto since 2011 and in this year alone, according to our records, has recieved 41 million rand. What exactly was that money for?
Momberg: The last time we got funding that the lottery paid I think it was somethng like 13 million was in March month of this year.

Not according to figures supplied by the lottery board. 24 millio rand in march, ten million in May and seven and a half million in July.

Momberg: Yes but according to that, there is documents that can prove that there was other organizations that hooked onto us that didn’t have their financials...
Bonita: Such as?
Momberg: We call them "babies". You understand? Organizations that we assist in terms of getting the instruments and...
Bonita: Okay who are these organizations?
Momberg? I'm not sure if I am liberty to give their names at this stage. I didn’t talk to them and you can at a later stage send me a request and I will submit it.

Which we did via email but got no response. We sent a follow up SMS. His response was that he was away and that he will try and arrange something. He is adamant that the applied for this funding for his own association and on behalf of some of his own troops.

We spoke to several of his minstrels, who told us that they had not known about these funds and received none of that lotto money. It seemed that they were too afraid to rock the boat. But one troop leader who regularly attends board meeting with Kevin Momberg and Richard Stemmet did speak to us and was amazed when we showed him the lotto records/. He asked for his identity to be concealed.
.
Troop leader: I feel they should be approached and we should get answers on why the troops don’t know about this.

We asked Kevin Momberg about a lottery payment of 12.93 million rand for a cultural museum.

Momberg: I’m not sure if that figure is correct but we intend doing, creating a museum, to the minstrel’s history and all that type of things.

But the troop owner we spoke to has never heard about this museum.

Troop Leader: Carnival Heritage Museum. This is the first that I hear of it. I don’t even know where this is going to be built or where this building is.

Meanwhile struggling welfare groups in Cape Town have slammed the decision of the lottery board over this 57 million rand payout and the city of Cape Town wants an investigation.

JP Smith Via Phone: Obviously the city is compelled to ensure any money that we give is fully and comprehensively audited for but we do believe that the situation with the approx. 57 million over the last few years that the minstrels have been given doesn't merit some investigation and we will be opening a case with the public protector.

Back on the streets under the sweltering sun, the dancing continued with Thaaqib showing no signs of slowing down. He was probably blissfully unaware of a major row brewing. Dolly is on the warpath.

Shahieda Thole: If it wasn’t for me going to the lotto to ask, nobody would have knew this guy is getting all this money.

She says that she was not even allocated enough busses for her troops. The other association, the Kaapse Klopse Karnval Association have received 5.1 million rand since 2011 but even one of their members is under investigation. She finds it very strange that one minstrel organization can be allotted so much lotto finding, 57 million rand, and she is determined to uncover the truth.

Shahieda Thole: I’m going to take them on. Ill start with the lotto and Ill finish with a lot of things, that he was part of, government money.

None of the various troops dare to challenge him because their troop with be ousted from the organization. Where does all the money go? Very few know that he has a factory that provides some of the uniforms and people are forced to buy these uniforms from him. It is in the contract. Meanwhile the City of Cape Town is demanding an audit from Mr, Stemmet. The ex gangster with time in jail, sneers at the 3 million given to them by the City of Cape Town and promises to provide an audit at some stage to the City of Cape Town. In the meantime, attempts have been made to get an audit from the lottery board who this year gave a whopping 16 million for this one day parade. They wont release this audit until they are given permission by this Stemmet man. Naturally he hasn't given permission. So behind all the glitz and glamor there is more than meets the eye. Of course the young boy who we feature will be oblivious to all of this. We investigate.
